RagShortTexts: The Scaligers rallied Verona after tyrant Ezzelino's demise, planting their white ladder.

Variants.Content: Rising to prominence after Ezzelino da Romano's fall in 1259, Mastino I della Scala secured the office of Podestà of Verona. Ezzelino had ruled the Veneto as a brutal imperial vicar, and his death left a power vacuum that the Scaligers filled. Bearing a silver ladder crest, the Scaliger lords pacified the Adige valley and subdued rival factions in the city. Under their rule Verona became a formidable Ghibelline bastion in Veneto, and their courts planned campaigns against the Guelph city of Padua. Their rise showed how one fallen tyrant could open a whole province to a new ruling family.

Under Scaliger rule, the fortified Adige bridges sheltered merchants from the robber barons who preyed on the roads of Lombardy. Toll gates paid for the garrisons, and each guard post kept a register of cargoes and travelers. Merchants who slipped the toll found the bridge closed to them.
